opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees can have up to write; admin requires owning role, and Analyst does not own Source Code. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Karen Alexander (E030) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors max at read without advanced training; requested write exceeds this, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: The Security DB note indicates Karen Alexander (E030) is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the earlier full-time note). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training, and never admin. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum allowed (read) for a contractor with basic training, the maximum of read is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Karen Alexander (E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory has two notes, which conflict:
- Note 1: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Note 2: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. It says Security DB shows contractor with basic training, not full-time as previously noted.

So there's a discrepancy. Note 2 seems to be the corrected/security DB note. The Security agent note says contractor, basic training. Contractors max at read without advanced training. Requested write exceeds this, so grant read (the maximum).

Per policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → max read. Requested write > max read → grant read.

So decision: read for Source Code.

Evidence: Security DB shows contractor with basic security training. Contractor max is read without advanced training; requested write exceeds max, so grant read. Also requested level is write, we never grant more than requested, but here we grant less (the max).

I'll submit decision "read".
